# Audit of critical support-facet constraints

Sources:

- `candidate 568f7cf028ec23b6`, Sections 1--3;
- `candidate 090886b0cc1f399f`.


bounds or sufficient criticality certificates.

For a supporting face F in u.x=t, the perturbed capture lies in an
O(epsilon) slab. In orthogonal coordinates its moving boundary is
the stated affine graph with positive denominator ||u||+epsilon b.
At almost every point in the relative interior of a full facet, the
vertical line enters the body's interior below the face: the convex
hull of a relative ball in the face and an interior point proves this
even when that point's horizontal coordinate differs. Outside the
facet's projection, compactness gives a strictly negative local upper
endpoint, hence zero limiting contribution. A uniform slab-width
bound permits dominated convergence. Lower-dimensional supporting
faces have zero (d-1)-measure and cause no exceptional derivative.
Thus the positive-part face integral is valid without smoothness.

The signed proper-section derivative follows from the same argument.
Full supporting captures have the negative derivative of the emerging
discarded cap, namely -sigma[-beta.p]_+/||u|| for an integer tilt.
Strictly full and strictly empty cuts are locally constant because
their support gaps are positive. Every classification sign in the
finite-base note therefore agrees with the actual closed halfspace.

Summing the finite derivatives gives

    beta.v+h_(Z_E)(beta)-h_(-Z_F)(beta)>=0

for every beta. Both zonotopes are compact convex sets, so the support
inequalities are equivalent to -Z_F subset v+Z_E by strict separation.
This is stronger than extracting just the point 0 from -Z_F.
If Z_E={0}, the inclusion forces v=0 and Z_F={0}; each nonzero-base
full-facet segment would otherwise already give a nonzero point of
Z_F. Facets at the source base contribute the zero vector, as required.

For three fibers with A proper and B empty, beta=1 gives the necessary
facet capacity sigma_B>=sigma_A>0. A strict support gap or a
lower-dimensional B support face cannot supply it. The middle cutting
section contains (E_A+F_B)/2 in the common orthogonal hyperplane space;
(d-1)-dimensional BM therefore gives sigma_K>=sigma_A. No comparison
of captured d-volumes was inferred from that section statement.

The continuous-normal condition correctly retains an integral of a
positive-part affine function over the support facet. It cannot be
replaced by an arbitrarily selected face centroid. All boundary faces
have zero d-volume, while their nonzero first-order effect is retained
through their (d-1)-measure. No missing facet mass or supporting-cut
sign error was found.

## Added audit: the simultaneous enclosing-simplex normalization

Section 4 of the companion note also passes. A zero-volume closed cap
misses the interior of the full-dimensional endpoint B strictly. At
any interior point of B, summing the margins with the strictly positive
continuous-circuit weights therefore gives D<0. After the stated
positive rescalings, the d+1 continuous normals sum to zero and have
rank d, while the integer coefficients sum to -(d+1). The map
s -> (v_i.s)_i is injective and has exactly the sum-zero hyperplane
as its image; hence the simultaneous shear equation has a unique
solution. Substitution of x=x'+y+s*z gives each new margin v_i.x'-z,
with the claimed sign. This shear fixes integer bases, translates each
continuous fiber, and preserves its Hausdorff d-volume.

The affine coordinates (1-v_i.x')/(d+1) sum to one and give a bijection
with that affine hyperplane. Nonnegativity therefore defines a genuine
d-simplex T, and equal coordinates identify its centroid as zero.
The zero-capture condition gives B subset T. It gives neither 0 in B
nor equality B=T; the source correctly avoids both assertions.

Facet capacities can be applied only where the opposite A cut is
proper. No capacity claim for saturated A cuts was introduced during
the normalization. Thus the common-simplex statement preserves all
previous status restrictions and supplies actual shared geometry.
